questions.question: The normal duration of human pregnancy from the first day of the last menstrual period is about:
questions.explanation: Naegele's rule: add 9 months and 7 days to the LMP to estimate the date of delivery.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The expected date of delivery by Naegele's rule is calculated by:

options.B: Adding 9 months and 7 days to the first day of the last menstrual period

questions.explanation: Assumes a regular 28-day cycle.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The hormone detected in a urine pregnancy test is:
questions.explanation: hCG is produced by the syncytiotrophoblast; levels double every 48 hours in early pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Anaemia in pregnancy is defined as a haemoglobin below:
questions.explanation: Severe anaemia is Hb < 7 g/dL; iron and folic acid supplementation are routine.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which cardiovascular change is normal in pregnancy?

options.C: Increase in cardiac output by 30–50% and fall in systemic vascular resistance

questions.explanation: Plasma volume increases more than red cell mass (physiological anaemia of pregnancy).
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Folic acid supplementation before conception and in early pregnancy is advised to prevent:
questions.explanation: Dose 400 µg daily (5 mg in high-risk women).
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pre-eclampsia is defined as new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks with:
questions.explanation: Severe features: BP ≥ 160/110, headache, visual disturbance, HELLP; treat with magnesium sulphate.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic seizures is:
questions.explanation: Monitor patellar reflexes, respiratory rate and urine output; calcium gluconate is the antidote.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Painless recurrent vaginal bleeding in the third trimester suggests:
questions.explanation: Digital vaginal examination is contraindicated; ultrasound confirms location.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Painful vaginal bleeding with a rigid tender uterus suggests:
questions.explanation: Risk factors: hypertension, trauma, smoking, cocaine.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest site of ectopic pregnancy is the:
questions.explanation: Classic triad: amenorrhoea, abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Gestational diabetes mellitus is screened for with a glucose tolerance test at:
questions.explanation: Risks: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, neonatal hypoglycaemia.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The third stage of labour is the stage of:

options.D: Expulsion of the placenta and membranes

questions.explanation: First stage: onset to full dilatation; second: full dilatation to delivery.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The correct sequence of the cardinal movements in labour begins with:

options.C: Engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, restitution

questions.explanation: Followed by external rotation and delivery of the shoulders.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The partograph is used to:

options.C: Monitor the progress of labour and fetal and maternal condition

questions.explanation: WHO partograph; the alert and action lines guide intervention.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage is:
questions.explanation: First-line: uterine massage and oxytocin; the 4 T's: tone, trauma, tissue, thrombin.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Apgar score assesses all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Components: appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration (scored 0–2 each); recorded at 1 and 5 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest type of breech presentation is:
questions.explanation: The buttocks present with hips flexed and knees extended.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The hormone responsible for the milk ejection (let-down) reflex is:
questions.explanation: Prolactin stimulates milk production.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The puerperium is the period of:

options.A: About 6 weeks after delivery during which the reproductive organs return to the non-pregnant state

questions.explanation: Involution of the uterus; lochia lasts up to 4–6 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which postnatal exercise is recommended to help restore pelvic floor function?

options.B: Pelvic floor (Kegel) contractions starting within the first days after delivery

questions.explanation: Also deep abdominal (transversus) activation and gradual return to activity.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Ovulation in a regular 28-day cycle occurs on about day:
questions.explanation: LH surge precedes ovulation by 24–36 hours.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The average age of menarche in India is about:
questions.explanation: Menopause occurs at about 45–50 years.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Polycystic ovary syndrome is characterised by:

options.C: Oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound

questions.explanation: Rotterdam criteria: two of three; associated with insulin resistance.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest cause of carcinoma cervix is:
questions.explanation: Screening by Pap smear and HPV testing; vaccination is preventive.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Endometriosis is defined as the presence of:

options.B: Endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity
options.D: Excess endometrial thickness within the uterus

questions.explanation: Presents with dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia and subfertility; chocolate cysts in the ovaries.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which change occurs after menopause?

options.D: Fall in oestrogen with rise in FSH and increased risk of osteoporosis

questions.explanation: Hot flushes, vaginal dryness and cardiovascular risk also increase.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Risk factors for uterovaginal prolapse include:

options.B: Multiparity, obesity, chronic cough and menopause

questions.explanation: Pelvic floor exercises are first-line for mild prolapse.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most effective reversible contraceptive method with a failure rate below 1% is:
questions.explanation: Combined oral pills have a typical-use failure rate of about 7–9%.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
